exposure: Early oral feeding after elective LSCS
Traditional delayed oral feeding after elective LSCS
outcome: Time to return of bowel function (first flatus, first stool)
Complication rates (nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, wound infections)
cohort: The study included women aged 18 to 40 years undergoing elective lower segment cesarean section (LSCS) with singleton pregnancies and gestational ages between 37 and 42 weeks.
finding: Early feeding after elective LSCS significantly enhanced recovery, leading to quicker return of bowel function, reduced hospital stay, and higher patient satisfaction without increasing complication rates.
